number.why: The numerical estimate 0.83 and 95% CI 0.75–0.93 are correct for overall intention-to-treat 28-day all-cause mortality comparing dexamethasone with usual care. However, unconditional SERVED_CONFIRMED is incorrect when scale is included: the source uses a Cox hazard ratio to estimate the mortality rate ratio, whereas served_outcome.estimand is OR and the adjudicated effect_object declares RISK_RATIO. The ruling acknowledges the distinction but leaves the incompatible scale binding confirmed.

quotes.span: Overall, 482 patients (22.9%) in the dexamethasone group and 1110 patients (25.7%) in the usual care group died within 28 days after randomization (age-adjusted rate ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75 to 0.93; P<0.001).
The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 28 days after randomization; further analyses were specified at 6 months.
All analyses were performed according to the intention-to-treat principle.
For the primary outcome of 28-day mortality, the hazard ratio from Cox regression was used to estimate the mortality rate ratio.

entry.why: Hospitalization with clinically suspected or laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 and systemic dexamethasone versus usual care are established. Adult-only eligibility is not established throughout recruitment because the minimum age was removed. This supports PARTLY without establishing that children actually entered this comparison. Usual care satisfies the question's comparator.

quotes.span: Hospitalized patients were eligible for the trial if they had clinically suspected or laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and no medical history that might, in the opinion of the attending clinician, put patients at substantial risk if they were to participate in the trial.
Initially, recruitment was limited to patients who were at least 18 years of age, but the age limit was removed starting on May 9, 2020.

Eligible and consenting patients were assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive either the usual standard of care alone or the usual standard of care plus oral or intravenous dexamethasone (at a dose of 6 mg once daily) for up to 10 days (or until hospital discharge if sooner) or to receive one of the other suitable and available treatments that were being evaluated in the trial.

missed: The decisive unresolved issue is the estimator binding, not the numerical triplet. The source explicitly states: "For the primary outcome of 28-day mortality, the hazard ratio from Cox regression was used to estimate the mortality rate ratio." (evidence/held/32678530/PMC7383595.xml). Retaining 0.83 (0.75–0.93) requires representing that estimator correctly; it does not validate an odds ratio or cumulative risk ratio.
